chunks: When a Section of them said: 'Why do you admonish a people whom God is about to destroy or to punish severely?' They replied: 'To clear ourselves of blame before your Lord, and that they may fear God.'

key_terms.أُمَّةٌ: A group or section of people

ai.seo_question: Why did the prophets continue to warn people if God had already decreed their destruction?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse clarifies the theological balance between divine omniscience and human free will, illustrating that prophets were sent not to alter God's ultimate decree but to fulfill the condition of 'clearing the messengers of blame' (ma'dhiratan). The dialogue reveals the skepticism of the people who questioned the utility of warning those destined for destruction, a theme central to the concept of *Adl* (Divine Justice) where the warning itself constitutes the trial. This narrative underscores the prophetic mission as a practical call to piety (*Taqwa*) rather than a mere announcement of fate.
